summary: PrS 86/43 contains both existing Preterit tokens and the existing Infinitiv example, under the page-based citations prs 255/34–35. No new example or citation correction is needed.

In PrS 9/21 the princess speaks a decapitation threat from inside. This context permits threatening behaviour but does not exclude the inherited gesture meaning; German rief is not a lexical definition of mhawalla.

The established construction has a threatening actor and a target marked by ʕal. PrS 9/21 lacks an overt ʕal target and supplies source m lalġul; omitted target arguments alone do not establish a new sense.
Does Mhawalla in PrS 9/21 denote a threatening gesture, verbal intimidation, or calling out? Confirm root and nuance before adding a verbal-threat subsense.
